descriptors.concept_name: Additional Conditions For An Offer For Sale For Issues Under Sub-Regulation (2) Of Regulation 8A
descriptors.definition: This principle governs the specific caps on shares offered for sale by pre-issue shareholders when a draft offer document is filed under regulation 6(2). It restricts large and small shareholders to specific percentages of their pre-issue fully diluted holdings and enforces strict lock-in requirements without exemptions.
inclusion: Shares offered by shareholders holding over twenty percent on a fully diluted basis
Shares offered by shareholders holding under twenty percent on a fully diluted basis
exclusion: Relaxations from lock-in under regulation 17 clause c for major shareholders
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard primary public issues by targeting secondary sales caps of existing stakeholders under specific regulatory entry routes.

descriptors.concept_name: Issue Of Convertible Debt Instruments And Warrants
descriptors.definition: This category encompasses the eligibility and regulatory frameworks governing the issuance of convertible debt instruments and warrants during initial public offerings. It sets prerequisites concerning default histories, credit ratings, and trustee appointments for issuers.
inclusion: Initial public offers featuring convertible debt instruments
Warrant issuance conditions tied to specified securities
exclusion: Pure equity-only initial public offers lacking hybrid conversion features
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from ordinary equity offerings by introducing debt-specific repayment, rating, and trusteeship mandates.

descriptors.concept_name: Eligibility Requirements For Issue Of Convertible Debt Instruments
descriptors.definition: An issuer may execute an initial public offer of convertible debt instruments without a prior public issue and listing of equity shares. However, eligibility requires that the issuer has not defaulted on interest or principal repayments for public debt instruments exceeding six months.
inclusion: Issuers proceeding directly to convertible debt instrument IPOs without prior equity listing
exclusion: Issuers with public debt repayment or interest defaults exceeding six months
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard equity IPO prerequisites by bypassing prior equity listing requirements while imposing strict debt servicing histories.

descriptors.concept_name: Additional Requirements For Issue Of Convertible Debt Instruments
descriptors.definition: Issuers executing an initial public offer of convertible debt instruments must fulfill supplementary safeguards including obtaining credit ratings, appointing debenture trustees, and maintaining appropriate debenture redemption reserves. Furthermore, if secured, the underlying assets must be free from encumbrances, fully cover the principal, and have proper pari passu or second charge consents.
inclusion: Appointment of certified debenture trustees
Creation of asset security and maintenance of debenture redemption reserves
exclusion: Unsecured debt instruments lacking asset charge configurations
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from basic eligibility criteria by focusing on post-eligibility structural security, trusteeship, and reserve creation obligations.

descriptors.concept_name: Conversion Of Optionally Convertible Debt Instruments Into Equity Shares
descriptors.definition: An issuer is prohibited from converting optionally convertible debt instruments into equity shares unless the holders provide explicit positive consent. Additionally, if the convertible portion exceeds ten crore rupees without pre-determined prices, investors must be granted an option not to convert.
inclusion: Written positive consent requirements for conversion
Non-conversion options for convertible portions exceeding ten crore rupees
exclusion: Situations where upper price limits and justifications are pre-determined and disclosed upfront
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from compulsorily convertible instruments by granting investors explicit opt-out rights and barring implied consent from silence.

descriptors.concept_name: Issue Of Convertible Debt Instruments For Financing
descriptors.definition: Issuers are restricted from utilizing convertible debt instruments to finance, grant loans to, or acquire shares of promoter group entities or group companies. An exception applies permitting fully convertible debt instruments for these objectives if the conversion timeline is under eighteen months.
inclusion: Fully convertible debt instruments with conversion periods under eighteen months applied to group financing
exclusion: Debt instruments with long-term conversion periods utilized for promoter group financing
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general corporate finance applications by imposing strict prohibitions and short conversion duration thresholds for intra-group funding.

descriptors.definition: Issuers may issue warrants during an initial public offer provided their tenure does not exceed eighteen months from allotment. The exercise price or its formula must be determined upfront with at least twenty-five per cent of the consideration collected initially, failing which unexercised warrant considerations are forfeited.
inclusion: Warrants attached to specified securities with a maximum eighteen-month tenure
Upfront collection of at least twenty-five per cent consideration
exclusion: Warrants exceeding the eighteen-month tenure limit
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from convertible debt instruments through specialized warrant tenure caps and mandatory upfront application money forfeiture rules.

descriptors.definition: This domain governs the mandatory minimum equity stake that promoters must maintain in an issuer following a public issue. It ensures structural alignment of promoter interests with public investors through specified post-issue capital thresholds.
inclusion: Regulatory constraints on promoter ownership percentages following initial public offerings
exclusion: Publicly held float portions outside promoter control
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general shareholding distributions by mandating specific baseline holding quotas enforceable at the time of an initial public offer.

descriptors.definition: Promoters must hold at least twenty per cent of the post-issue capital, with qualified institutional entities permitted to bridge shortfalls up to ten per cent if promoters fall short. Promoters fulfill this via equity or convertible securities, subject to specific pricing rules, though the requirement is waived if the issuer has no identifiable promoter.
inclusion: Promoter capital contribution via equity or convertible securities
Shortfall coverage by specified institutional investors up to ten per cent
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard shareholding by imposing mandatory statutory minimum ownership rules and conditional institutional top-up mechanisms.

descriptors.definition: This framework restricts the transferability of specified securities held by promoters and other pre-issue stakeholders for designated statutory periods following an initial public offer. It ensures stability by preventing premature liquidation of core stakeholder holdings.
inclusion: Restrictions prohibiting the transfer of promoter securities post-IPO
exclusion: Freely tradable post-issue public share allocations
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from ongoing continuous listing disclosure rules by imposing temporary transfer freezes specifically tied to the timeline of an initial public offering.

descriptors.concept_name: Lock-in of specified securities held by the promoters (Regulation 16)
descriptors.definition: The minimum promoter contribution is locked-in for eighteen months, extending to three years if the majority of issue proceeds are utilized for capital expenditure. Promoter holdings exceeding the minimum contribution are locked-in for six months, extending to one year under capital expenditure utilization conditions.
inclusion: Eighteen-month and three-year lock-in tiers for minimum promoter contributions
Six-month and one-year lock-in tiers for excess promoter holdings
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general pre-issue capital lock-ins by applying differentiated duration tiers based on whether issue proceeds fund capital expenditures.

descriptors.concept_name: Lock-in of specified securities held by persons other than the promoters (Regulation 17)
descriptors.definition: The entire pre-issue capital held by non-promoters must be locked-in for six months from the initial public offer allotment date. Specific exemptions apply to employee stock option shares, employee trust transfers, and holdings by venture capital or alternative investment funds subject to prior holding period calculations.
inclusion: Non-promoter pre-issue capital subject to six-month lock-in
Exemptions for venture capital funds, alternative investment funds, and employee stock schemes
exclusion: Promoter-held specified securities governed separately under regulation 16
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from promoter lock-in requirements by targeting non-promoter equity and providing targeted exemptions for institutional venture investors and employee benefit trusts.
